This arithmetic does not establish the effect of switching a case from B to A. The counts specify neither an assignment mechanism nor both outcomes for the same case. The descriptive comparison holds under stated weights; a causal claim needs more information.

draft3: Sela put the return ticket beside her father's letter. The ticket named a route home. The letter said: Tell us where you are. Below the five words, the page was blank. After three weeks away, she could read them as a request for a place or a request to come back.

Her coastal map lay across the drawing board. Each inlet had its name, but the rooming house where she worked was too small to appear. Through the window she could see the harbor at the center of the sheet. The view supplied no further sentence from her father.

Sela took a second copy and marked the rooming house with a dot. She wrote the street beside it. Her first fold ran through the dot; she tried another. Then she put the map into an envelope and addressed it to her father. She could send this answer without claiming to have answered both questions.

The ticket went back into the drawer. In the morning, Sela carried the envelope to the postbox and let it drop. At her desk she returned to the northern edge of the first map, where her pencil lines stopped. No reply had arrived. She sharpened the pencil but added no coast beyond them.
